statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 11% (low), Stress 50% (elevated), Confidence 87% (high). Nasdaq-100 futures are still rotating inside the narrow overnight band with the low intact, and VIX, Treasury yields and crude show no amplifier alignment ahead of the Jackson Hole keynote.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping keeps the published state at EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Stress is carried at 50% because three high-impact U.S. items print simultaneously at 14:00 UTC. The published danger window is narrow and evidence-based, covering 13:30-16:00 UTC from the cash open through the plausible delayed second leg; the conditional path maps to WATCH for the 14:00 and 15:00 UTC hours only. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold the overnight band low as single-name damage offsets Nvidia before Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Thursday at 29,641.56, up 1.43% and just below its 29,643.53 session high, after Nvidia rose almost 9% on a revenue outlook well above consensus. Overnight the leadership has been partly given back at the single-name level rather than at the index level: PayPal fell about 12% after Stripe and Advent stepped away from an acquisition proposal, Marvell fell close to 8% on soft third-quarter margin guidance despite raising its full-year outlook, and IREN fell about 9% on a revenue miss, while Affirm rose about 11%. NQ futures have spent the whole overnight session inside a 29,592-29,707 band roughly 0.39% wide and were last at 29,611.25, down 0.28% against a 29,695.75 prior settlement. The band low has held through six hours, retracements have repeatedly occurred, and there is no chain of failed pullbacks or extension from a session extreme, so the structure is orderly two-way rotation rather than directional efficiency. Cross-assets provide no amplifier: VIX closed at 14.51, down 4.6%; the 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields are near 4.24% and 4.68%, each up under a basis point on the day; and crude is softer, with WTI near $82.92 and Brent near $88.03 as Persian Gulf supply continues to recover. The concentrated risk of the day is scheduled rather than observed. Fed Chair Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote at 14:00 UTC, at the same instant as the BLS preliminary payroll benchmark revision and final Michigan sentiment, with Chicago PMI 15 minutes earlier and the cash open at 13:30 UTC. Consistent with the published risk definitions, scheduled event importance and wide implied moves raise Stress and lower Confidence rather than Tail; Tail rises only on an observed price path that denies retracement, and none is observed at the assessment cutoff. Tail is therefore held at 11% with Stress at 50%. The conditional path lifts Tail to 22% and 21% for the 14:00 and 15:00 UTC hours to reflect the multi-stage keynote and a plausible delayed second leg in the long end, then decays on the assumption of orderly price discovery. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekend halt removes any live price path, so the remaining slots are published as a flat closed-market state with reduced Confidence.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 clock-hours every published Claude assessment stayed in the EA_ON band, with Tail between 10% and 14% and Stress ranging from the mid-40s during the European morning to the low 50s around the U.S. session and overnight. The dominant mode was predominantly mixed, with two trend-up marks at 17:00 and 20:00 UTC on 27 August as the Nvidia-led advance extended into the cash close, and one unavailable hour at 09:00 UTC where no assessment was published. Confidence held between 82% and 88% throughout. The series describes a firm but orderly advance followed by a narrow, mean-reverting overnight session, with no hour at which persistent no-retracement structure was recorded.
outlookSummary: The horizon runs from the late-Asian handover through the European morning into a concentrated U.S. afternoon and then the weekend futures halt. Conditional risk drifts up from the 07:00 UTC European open, steps up at the 13:30 UTC cash open and 13:45 UTC Chicago PMI, and peaks across 14:00-15:00 UTC on the Warsh keynote, the payroll benchmark revision and final Michigan sentiment, where the mapped state moves to WATCH for two hours. It then decays through the U.S. afternoon on the assumption of orderly price discovery, with a modest step up for the closing auction and weekend risk reduction ahead of Monday's month-end. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekend halt leaves no live price path, so the final nine slots are published as a flat closed-market state with reduced Confidence. Every score beyond the current hour is conditional risk, not an assertion that any future structure has already been observed.
